(Aug 2026) impossibility result - no bounded-degree coordinate-free QUBO can enforce 2D containment - settles our encoding (coordinate-based set-packing for disk scaffolds). QAL-BP (Cellini 2024) analytical penalty estimation transfers to our scaffold QUBO. Cepaite et al. (Phasecraft, Aug 2026) warm-start theory gives our protocol template (Q-factor, beat-uniform-random bar). Gap confirmed: all warm-start work is discrete->discrete; nobody has warm-started continuous geometric optimization from QA samples. Top risks: 16x16-grid scaffold QUBO (~3k dense vars) won't embed on bare Advantage2 (hybrid/SimCIM from start); no demonstrated quantum edge in warm-start quality for packing; grid-resolution vs fidelity tension unknown.

decision: review complete; encoding choice settled, Q01 scoped

text: Q01: QUBO-optimized scaffolds do NOT improve hardening (null). Classical SA on 100-var disk-packing QUBO produced 16 valid scaffolds; warm-started harden (n=16) vs random-init control (n=16) on squ n=11. Mean final L: QUBO 3.9291 vs control 3.9173 — QUBO WORSE on average (one-sided Mann-Whitney p=0.96, fails p<0.05). QUBO's best (3.8771) beats control's best (3.8894), but the distribution is worse. Interpretation: QUBO optimizes disk tightness, but fidelity (arrangement vs optimum) is what matters; the warm start may constrain rather than help. The 'better scaffold sampling improves outcomes' hypothesis is not supported by this test.

decision: null; QUBO scaffolds worse on average
